summary: Yutaka Kanazawa specializes in Buddhist studies and earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2010. Kanazawa studied under Kogi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu, with Shoryu Katsura as doctoral supervisor and Masaaki Noni as co-supervisor.
Yutaka Kawasaki works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seio Okuda and held an attested post at the University of Tokyo in 2024.

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania, learning under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Louis Renou, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He served at Kyoto University and Collège de France.

Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science from around 1948 to 1951, and served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1968 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) specializes in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Education, and Hitotsubashi University, later holding posts at Hitotsubashi and Kyoto University.

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He held academic posts at Kyoritsu University of Pharmacy and Kanagawa University.

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) was a sinologist and linguist who studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under doctoral supervisor August Conrady. He held a post at Peking University from circa 1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura specializes in Indology and linguistics. Kawamura was a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University from 2015 to 2018, with affiliations attested at Hiroshima University (2013–2020) and the University of Oxford (2019).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) specialized in sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University, and held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, the University of Tokyo, and Daito Bunka University.

Yün-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, having studied under Tan Yun-shan. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later served as a professor at McMaster University.

Yōzō Taniyama (born 1972) works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tohoku University (~1992–1996), he later held posts there, as well as at International Buddhist University, St. Thomas University, Japan, and Sophia University.

Zarawar Khan specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Khan completed an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

Zawgyi (1907–1990) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Rangoon from circa 1924 to 1929, where he studied under Pe Maung Tin, and later attended the University of Dublin from circa 1934 to 1936.

Zayn Kassam works in religious studies and philosophy, having earned a B.A. from McGill University in 1977. Kassam's posts include positions at Pomona College beginning in 1995, the Pacific Basin Institute, and the Institute of Ismaili Studies.

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan in 2001 under Donald S. Lopez, Jr. He held a post at the College of Charleston.

Zellig Harris (1909–1992) was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1928 to 1934. He held academic posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University (~1946–1947).

Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Yang studied at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies under Toshinori Ochiai and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1934 to 1937 under Naoshiro Tsuji.
Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Shibayama held posts at Otani University and Hanazono University.
Zenno Ikuno specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Ikuno earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).
